title: The summary for Friday 27 November
text:
Good morning, it is Friday 27 November: this is the GERICO summary.

In Kuwait, two Italian technicians aged 65 and 36 died on Thursday in a drone attack. They were working on the maintenance of an anti-aircraft defence system. Kuwait attributes the attack to Iran, which denies having launched the drone.

In Brussels, the European summit on the budget from 2028 to 2034 closed without an agreement. The President of the European Council, Costa, is asking for an agreement by the end of the year. Twenty-four countries support the 45-billion-euro loan to Ukraine.

Eurozone leaders have agreed on the appointment of Spaniard Pablo Hernández de Cos to the presidency of the ECB, replacing Christine Lagarde. The formal appointment comes in December.

In Saudi Arabia, the Houthis have hit the Jazan refinery: one worker has died. In New Zealand, the centre-right government is one seat away from a majority.

Moving on to the markets. Yesterday, European stock markets closed sharply higher, with Wall Street closed for Thanksgiving. Piazza Affari gains more than two points, London and Paris rise between one and a half and two points. The spread between BTPs and Bunds falls to 107 points. WTI crude is at 84 dollars, Brent at nearly 95. This morning, Tokyo and Hong Kong are rising.

There are no high-impact events today. At eight forty-five, France's preliminary GDP and inflation are released; at fourteen thirty, the US trade balance.

The full news, with sources, is on GERICO. No investment advice.
